name: sextractor
desc: Extract catalogs of sources from astronomical images
why: Real astronomy software that turns telescope images into source catalogues, a genuinely runnable piece of science at home.

brief.what_it_is: SExtractor is a program that builds a catalogue of objects from an astronomical image. It takes in astronomical images and writes out a catalogue of detected sources, with measurements for each one. The homepage says it is particularly oriented towards reduction of large-scale galaxy-survey data, but it can also perform reasonably well on moderately crowded star fields. The Homebrew entry lists two executables, sex and ldactoasc; the fetched pages did not describe what ldactoasc does.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes SExtractor as software for extracting catalogs of sources from astronomical images, short for 'Source Extractor'. The homepage frames it as a pipeline tool in the AstrOmatic suite, written by Emmanuel Bertin.
brief.how_it_works: The fetched pages describe the processing stages only as section headings in the user manual: input and output files, a configuration file, a catalog parameter file, background modelling, weighting, flagging, isophotal and windowed positional measurements, aperture photometry, and model fitting. The mechanism itself was not explained in the text I read.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond Homebrew was confirmed. The user manual's contents list includes 'Installing the software' and 'Hardware requirements' sections, but I did not retrieve their text. The homepage points to 'Binaries' and 'Source' downloads, which I did not open.
brief.standout: It is a long-standing, widely cited source-extraction tool from the 1996 Bertin & Arnouts paper, and it is a real piece of astronomy software a reader could run on their own telescope images. The homepage also notes its packaging changed in 2009 and that it can write XML-VOTable metadata.
brief.status: Unknown, leaning maintained. The GitHub README carries live CI and documentation badges, and the online manual is labelled SExtractor 2.28.0. The homepage's newest news post is dated 2014-03-20, and I did not find a last-release or last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The homepage says the official documentation 'is unfortunately still far from complete' and points to a third-party manual instead. The Homebrew caveats field is empty. I did not check the license, which the manual lists in a section I did not read. The sample command lines and build steps were not visible in the pages I fetched, so the brief has no verbatim commands.
